text: Cloud Security Posture Management, or CSPM, is a category of tooling that continuously scans a cloud environment -- every storage account, every security group, every IAM policy -- and compares what it finds against a security best-practice baseline. It isn't looking for a bug in an application's code. It's looking for a setting that's wrong: something left open, left unencrypted, or left with more access than it needs. That distinction matters, because it's exactly where a huge share of real cloud security incidents actually start.

This program already covered vulnerability scanning: tools that find a flaw in code, like an unpatched CVE with a CVSS score, and tell you to patch it. CSPM is that same continuous-scanning idea applied to a different layer. Instead of asking 'is this software out of date,' it asks 'is this resource configured safely.' A storage bucket set to public, a security group open to the entire internet -- none of those are a CVE. They're a configuration choice, and CSPM exists to catch them the same way a scanner catches an unpatched flaw.

A CSPM tool runs the same cycle on repeat. First it discovers every resource in the environment -- it has to see everything before it can check anything. Then it compares each one against a baseline, usually a recognized benchmark like CIS. Anything that doesn't match gets flagged as a finding. And then it does the whole thing again, on a schedule, because cloud environments change constantly -- a setting that was safe yesterday can be flipped open by someone's change today.

That continuous re-scanning matters because of how cloud breaches actually happen in practice. Look at the post-incident write-ups behind most publicized cloud breaches and the pattern repeats: it usually wasn't a novel exploit or a sophisticated attack chain. It was a resource that was simply left misconfigured -- a bucket, a permission, an open port -- sitting there until someone found it. CSPM's entire job is to be the one who finds it first, continuously, before an attacker does.

So CSPM means continuous scanning for configuration risk, not code vulnerabilities, against a security baseline, because misconfiguration is where most real cloud incidents start.
